thesis: Tenaga has a verified cost-inclusive income bridge: RM1.8018bn cash after the specified asset, finance and lease payments covers RM1.6322bn dividends. Neither side decisively resolves whether that narrow RM169.6m buffer adequately compensates RM60.936bn borrowings and RM31.198bn leases at 16.83x trailing earnings. Modestly rising H1 operating profit supports ownership while weaker reported earnings and heavy investment prevent a clear increase call.
strongest_counterexample: The conservative cash bridge already includes interest, lease principal and lease interest; the payout is observed to be covered, and H1 operating profit increased to RM4.539bn despite adverse FX comparison.
invalidation_conditions: A comparable H1 post-finance/lease cash surplus below dividends would invalidate the current funded-income counterweight.
Comparable H1 post-finance/lease cash above RM1.8018bn with borrowings below RM60.936bn and Q2 operating margin above 11.44% would strengthen the ownership case enough to reopen neutral.
decisive_factors: Cash capacity is verified rather than an extraction gap.
Thin payout coverage and large obligations offset operating resilience; broad deposits include restrictions and longer tenors.
